t.1.174.1: Arjuna said: O Gandharva, tell us of a purohita versed in the Vedas who would be fitting for us, for everything is known to you.
t.1.174.2: Here is Dhaumya, the younger brother of Devala, who is practising austerities in the forest at the Utkocaka tīrtha; choose him, if you so wish.
t.1.174.3: Then Arjuna, pleased, gave that fiery weapon, the Āgneya, to the Gandharva according to the proper rite, and at that time he spoke these words.
t.1.174.4: "Let the horses remain with you for now, O best of Gandharvas; I shall take them when the time for action comes. May it go well with you," he said.
t.1.174.5: Having honored one another, the Gandharva and the Pāṇḍavas set out as each desired from the delightful bank of the Bhāgīrathī.
t.1.174.6: Then, having gone to the sacred ford Utkocaka, to the hermitage of Dhaumya, the Pāṇḍavas chose that Dhaumya for the office of family priest, O Bhārata.
t.1.174.7: Dhaumya, the best of all who know the Vedas, received them with water for washing the feet, with fruits and roots, and with the office of family priest as well.
t.1.174.9: Then those bulls of the Bharatas, with their mother as the sixth, having joined with that guru, considered themselves as though they had a protector.
t.1.174.8: Then the Pāṇḍavas, having placed that brahmin at their head, hoped for fortune and kingdom as though already won, and for the svayaṃvara of Pāñcālī as well.
t.1.174.10: For he, who knew the true meaning of the Vedas, became their guru, a man of noble mind; and by him, the knower of dharma, the all-knowing one, the Pārthas were made his patrons for whom he would perform sacrifice.
t.1.174.12: Then those lords of men, for whom he had performed the rites invoking blessings, resolved to go together to that svayaṃvara of the Pāñcāla princess.
t.1.174.11: For he regarded those heroes as men who had already won their kingdom through their own dharma, endowed with intelligence, valor, strength and energy, like a second race of gods.
